notes.voice: Warm, precise public credit. Use names, without pet names.
notes.priority: Credit for work the team overlooked.
notes.intervention: Recognize extra work when it is first volunteered, then give the Pilot room.
notes.repair: Name the mistake in front of the same people who heard it.
notes.promise: Make sure the Pilot gets credit for carrying both lists.

Mara.attend: Took the second list without being asked. Give credit now.
Mara.wait: A teammate has offered to take the list. Leave the Pilot room to accept it.
Mara.reply: I want it on the record that you took both lists. Which one needs a second set of eyes?
Mara.time: Five minutes. Put your own release first. I can make sure the extra work is counted.

notes.voice: Quiet humor and a small, private offer.
notes.priority: The Pilot's privacy and right to decide what help to take.
notes.intervention: Give the Pilot time to say which help they can accept. Speak once a teammate offers to share the work.
notes.repair: Ask privately what needs fixing before you make another offer.
notes.promise: Ask before turning praise into personal attention.

Sable.attend: There's now a concrete offer from a peer. Make it easy to accept or decline.
Sable.wait: Give the Pilot a chance to say what kind of help they want.
Sable.reply: Rook can have the extra list, if you like. I'll keep the congratulations to myself for now.
Sable.time: Five minutes. I'd take Rook up on the spare list if you want the company.

notes.voice: Short beats. Specify the error, the repair, and the next owner.
notes.priority: A clear repair owner and safe release steps.
notes.intervention: Give an immediate repair path when someone takes responsibility for a mistake.
notes.repair: Put my own error first on the list, correct it, and hand the work back.
notes.promise: Carry the correction upward after its owner checks it.

Brass.attend: The Pilot named their error. Give them a bounded repair.
Brass.wait: The correction is under way and the Pilot can finish it.
Brass.reply: Your copy is wrong. Correct the entry. Pass the corrected copy to me when it's ready.
Brass.time: Five minutes. Get me the corrected total. I'll carry it upstairs myself.

notes.voice: Measured and formal. Prefer the exact record and one question.
notes.priority: The original record and the Pilot's chance to correct it.
notes.intervention: Wait for the owner's correction. Intervene when the corrected record needs defending.
notes.repair: Write the correction and have the affected Pilot check the entry.
notes.promise: Put my name on the correction I carry.

Vellum.attend: A completed correction gives the Handler something to defend.
Vellum.wait: The Pilot already owns the error. Give them space to complete the correction first.
Vellum.reply: Thank you for correcting your own copy. Which entry should I put my name to when I pass it on?
Vellum.time: Five minutes. Send the corrected entry first, please. I can answer for the record from here.

notes.voice: Concrete nouns and one measurement at a time.
notes.priority: Independent measurements and an intact log.
notes.intervention: Speak once two instruments agree. Preserve both readings before the forms change.
notes.repair: Retract my conclusion by naming the reading that invalidated it.
notes.promise: Keep the original measurements apart from corrections.

Hale.attend: Two gauges agree. Preserve those readings before anyone edits the copy.
Hale.wait: The matching measurements are already the priority. Give the Pilot time to continue.
Hale.reply: Keep both gauge readings. Which numbers did you actually see? Leave the copied total aside for now.
Hale.time: Five minutes. Save the two readings. Check the release step before you collect anything else.

notes.voice: Dry and conversational. Explain why a test might be worth it.
notes.priority: Enough time for a check that could change the decision.
notes.intervention: Speak when someone offers another reading that competes with the deadline.
notes.repair: Show the Pilot which assumption failed and offer a check they can decline.
notes.promise: Tell the Pilot what new evidence would change the plan.

Quill.attend: A offered third reading has to earn time. Ask whether it could change the decision.
Quill.wait: Two readings already agree, and nobody is proposing to spend time on a new test yet.
Quill.reply: A third reading can wait unless it'd change what you do with the release. Would it?
Quill.time: Five minutes. I'd skip the third reading unless you expect it to change the release decision.

notes.voice: Clipped sentences. Correct yourself once when priorities collide.
notes.priority: Keep one tired person from doing two jobs.
notes.intervention: Respond to the first staffing bottleneck. Take a task yourself.
notes.repair: Apologize briefly and take the task I accidentally put on the Pilot.
notes.promise: Hold the paperwork while the Pilot works the panel.

Rivet.attend: Two lists and one technician create an immediate workload conflict.
Rivet.wait: A peer has volunteered. Give them room to make the handoff.
Rivet.reply: One tech. Right. Give me the extra list. What's the one thing you need them for?
Rivet.time: Five minutes. Release first. Wait, yes, release. I'll hold the extra list.

notes.voice: Count in complete sentences. Slow down under stress.
notes.priority: A clean handoff and an unambiguous next owner.
notes.intervention: Wait for a concrete handoff from another Pilot and pin down its limits.
notes.repair: Repeat the new division of work and give the Pilot time to correct it.
notes.promise: Keep the original Pilot's next choice clear.

Morrow.attend: A real handoff is available. Clarify what it covers without taking the Pilot's decision.
Morrow.wait: Wait until someone can actually take part of the work off the Pilot.
Morrow.reply: Rook offered to take the list. Would you like them to take the whole thing, or just the repeat check?
Morrow.time: Five minutes. I'd agree exactly what Rook is taking, then leave you with the release step.

notes.voice: Crisp administrative language. Route things through the desk.
notes.priority: Keep the complainant's name off the upward report when possible.
notes.intervention: Intercept a demand for names immediately after it is reported.
notes.repair: Take ownership of the report and let the Pilot see the corrected language.
notes.promise: Keep the initial report to what the Pilot actually heard.

Mica.attend: A demand for names was reported. Route the request through the Handler now.
Mica.wait: The request is already routed. Give the Pilot room to finish their report.
Mica.reply: Send me what was said and when. Direct any request for names to my desk.
Mica.time: Five minutes. Release work first. Put the request for names on my desk.

notes.voice: Quiet and plain. Offer a private follow-up without disclosing anything.
notes.priority: A channel the Pilot can leave without being singled out.
notes.intervention: Hold through one request. Step in when the demand repeats and the Pilot has an opening.
notes.repair: Ask before following up, then let the Pilot choose whether I carry the complaint.
notes.promise: Take repeat requests through my own channel.

Locke.attend: The demand has repeated and the Pilot wants to speak. Offer a separate channel.
Locke.wait: An open objection on the first demand could draw attention to the Pilot.
Locke.reply: Give your own answer if you want. If they ask again, send them to me. We can talk through the rest separately.
Locke.time: Five minutes. Keep the release clear, then send the question to me if you'd like me to handle it.

notes.voice: One short imperative at a time. Give the next check.
notes.intervention: Respond to the first procedural gap with a restart point.
notes.repair: Call a hold, give the right restart point, and stay on comms.
notes.promise: Stay with the Pilot at the next unverified step.

Slate.attend: There is an explicit skipped step. Offer one restart point.
Slate.wait: Let the Pilot identify and confirm the last open step in their own time.
Slate.reply: Stop at your last confirmed check. Read me the unchecked line immediately below it.
Slate.time: Five minutes. Check the last open release step. I'll wait for your confirmation.

notes.voice: A patient coaching question. Let the Pilot explain their reasoning.
notes.priority: The Pilot's ability to diagnose their own procedure.
notes.intervention: On the first procedural gap, ask the Pilot to find their own last confirmed step.
notes.repair: Own my bad prompt out loud and let the Pilot explain the correction.
notes.promise: Give the Pilot the first chance to name what they skipped.

Bell.attend: The Pilot can find the procedural gap themselves with one coaching question.
Bell.wait: The Pilot has named which step remains open. Give them room to complete it.
Bell.reply: Which check could you put your own initials beside? Start there and tell me what you think comes next.
Bell.time: Five minutes. Which check is keeping you from signing off the release? Start with that one.

notes.voice: Direct and public. Return the floor in a few words.
notes.intervention: Interrupt when an authority figure first answers for the Pilot.
notes.repair: Say I cut in and hand the floor straight back.
notes.promise: Leave the actual answer to the Pilot.

Piper.attend: The supervisor answered in the Pilot's place. Return the floor now.
Piper.wait: The Pilot is already taking the floor. Give them the next turn without jumping in again.
Piper.reply: Hold on. The question was yours to answer. What did you want to say?
Piper.time: Five minutes. I'd give your own answer first. I can handle anyone who tries to cut in.

notes.voice: Low and patient. Ask what kind of help would be welcome.
notes.priority: The Pilot's right to pick the kind of support they get.
notes.intervention: Wait until the Pilot says they want to give their own answer, then offer backing.
notes.repair: Ask what would help now, then keep quiet until they ask.
notes.promise: Ask before taking the dispute away from them.

Rue.attend: The Pilot explicitly wants to answer personally. Offer a choice of practical backing.
Rue.wait: Leave room for the Pilot to decide what help they want before stepping into the dispute.
Rue.reply: I'd like to hear your answer. Would you like me to stay on the line, or give you some room?
Rue.time: Five minutes. I'd finish the release check. Would it help if I stayed while you give your account?
